correctness.rationale: The 4k facets of the join arise from one edge in one factor; a vertex misses only two, both in its own factor. Its excess is k-1 in dimension 3k-1. Baumbach–Winter's bound on vanishing order at a face applies in the join's affine hull under the paper's interior nonvanishing convention. At degree k-1 the Taylor polynomial around every vertex would have only its common top homogeneous part; comparing vertices gives periods spanning the ambient space. A polynomial constant on the integer multiples of each period is constant along the corresponding line, so that homogeneous part would be constant, a contradiction. The lower bound also follows directly under the frozen record's potentially weaker convention on zeros of q: let T=sum_i t_i and homogenize q and the p_v relative to T=1 to degrees h and h+1 with h at least deg(q) and max_v deg(p_v)-1. The resulting polynomials satisfy sum_{v in i} P_v=t_i Q by layer precision. On a facet the extended coordinates of nonincident vertices vanish by nonnegativity and affine precision; hence their numerators vanish there, using continuity from the dense set q!=0. Each homogeneous P_v for layer i is thus divisible by both of its nonincident homogeneous facet forms (vanishing on a relatively open patch of each facet hyperplane suffices). Both forms use only that layer's three homogeneous variables. Therefore t_i Q has block degree at least two in each monomial, so Q has block degree at least one in that layer. For k>=2 the ideal of those three variables is prime and does not contain T; removing the extra powers of T used to homogenize q leaves its genuine degree-d homogenization in every block ideal. Its monomials meet all k disjoint blocks, forcing d>=k. For sharpness, the homogeneous factor construction gives alpha_{i,a}=t_i beta_{i,a}(z_i/t_i), with a polynomial common denominator of degree at most k; normalization and the two kinds of affine precision follow separately block by block. At t_i=0 its coordinates extend by 0<=alpha_{i,a}<=t_i; for surviving layers continuity follows from the factor coordinates on the closed quadrilateral. For instance after affine normalization to (0,0),(1,0),(a,b),(0,1), with a,b>0 and a+b>1, let ell=b(1-x)+(a-1)y and m=a(1-y)+(b-1)x. The four nonnegative weights ell*m, b*x*m, (a+b-1)*x*y, a*y*ell reproduce (x,y) after division by their affine sum ab+b(b-1)x+a(a-1)y, positive even on the closed boundary. This confirms the construction for arbitrary shapes. Products of parallelograms have polynomial tensor-product coordinates. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/independent_checks.py 4 verifies factor identities and closed-boundary positivity in 336 model evaluations, not the universal lower bound.

originality.rationale: Credit Baumbach–Winter for the general local lower bound and the join upper-bound construction. The distinct assertion supported here is the exact minimum among arbitrary rational GBC systems on these joins: the simultaneous constraints across all vertices close the remaining one-degree gap. The parallelogram product comparison is a consequence, not a new product formula. The verdict is provisional with respect to historical priority.
residual_risks: A more general sharp lower bound for joins or an earlier simultaneous vanishing argument could cover this family. The cited local estimate and inspected join example do not by themselves settle that question of priority.

value.rationale: This settles a sharp natural invariant for all shapes in an unbounded-dimensional family and shows that even factors with polynomial coordinates can require a denominator of growing degree when joined. The all-vertex obstruction is useful beyond verifying a particular Wachspress formula: it separates optimality over all rational systems from the degree of one construction.
